import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

**Task:** call your app's methods from a frontend or a script with types checked
by the compiler, and find out before publishing whether a new version breaks
the clients already out there.

Every app embeds its [ABI](/core/build/app-abi/): its methods, their parameters
and results, its errors and events. `mero-app-build codegen` turns it into an
OpenAPI 3.1 document and a thin typed client over the client you already use:
mero-js's `CalimeroClient` (its `client.apps.call` and `client.apps.view`) or
calimero-client-py's `Client` (its `client.apps.call` and `client.apps.view`,
answering JSON). They keep doing the
work (the attested, sealed channel, sessions, passkey step-ups, retries); the
generated code only adds the method names and types.

## Generate a client

Put `mero-app-build` on PATH once (`scripts/install-mero-app-build.sh`), build
the app, then point `codegen` at the component, the `.mpk` bundle or an ABI JSON
file (`meroctl context abi` saves an installed app's):

```bash
mero-app-build apps/kv-store --out kv-store.wasm
mero-app-build codegen --abi kv-store.wasm --lang ts -o src/generated
```

```
wrote src/generated/openapi.json
wrote src/generated/client.ts
```

`--lang` is `ts`, `python` or `openapi` (the document alone). Every language
writes `openapi.json` beside the client. The client class is named after
`--name`, else the package of an `.mpk` or the file's name (`kv-store.wasm` gives
`KvStoreClient`). A multi-service bundle writes one directory per service;
`--service <name>` picks one.

## Use it from TypeScript

```ts
import { CalimeroClient, passkeyConfirm } from '@calimero-network/mero-js';
import { KvStoreClient } from './generated/client';

const client = /* a signed-in CalimeroClient */;
const kv = new KvStoreClient(client, appId);

await kv.set({ key: 'greeting', value: 'hello' });
const value: string | null = await kv.get({ key: 'greeting' });
const count: string = await kv.len(); // u64: a decimal string

for await (const event of kv.events()) {
  if (event.kind === 'Inserted') console.log(event.data.key, event.data.value);
}
```

A call takes `{ idempotencyKey, confirm, signal }` as its last argument, a view
`{ consistency, minIndex, signal }` (`consistency: 'stale'` reads the replica that
answers). A `confirm` method's `412 CONFIRM_REQUIRED` step-up is answered by the
call's `confirm`, else by the `confirm` the `CalimeroClient` was built with
(here `rooms` is `apps/rooms`' generated client):

```ts
await rooms.adminRelease({ id, reason }, { confirm: passkeyConfirm(passkey) });
```

An `option<..>` argument may be left out or be `null`: the SDK reads both as
`None`. In an error's or an event's fields it is always there, `null` for none.

### Keep a refreshed session

mero-js refreshes an expired session on its own, and has no event that says it
did. A page that stores the session passes `after`, which runs after every call
and view, refused ones included:

```ts
const kv = new KvStoreClient(client, appId, {
  after: () => saveSession(client.session),
});
```

### Test without a node

The class takes an `AppTransport`, the part of `CalimeroClient` it uses
(`apps.call`, `apps.view`, `events`), so a test double implements that alone:

```ts
const kv = new KvStoreClient(
  {
    apps: {
      call: async () => ({ result: null }),
      view: async ({ method }) => ({ result: method === 'len' ? '0' : null }),
    },
    async *events() {},
  },
  'app-1',
);
```

## Use it from Python

```python
from calimero import Client
from generated.client import KvStoreClient

kv = KvStoreClient(client, app_id)  # a signed-in calimero Client
kv.set("greeting", "hello")
assert kv.get("greeting") == "hello"
assert kv.len(consistency="stale") == "1"
rooms.admin_release("b-1", "late", passkey=passkey)  # apps/rooms' confirm method
```

Arguments are keyword arguments in snake_case (`room_id=`); errors and events
are `TypedDict`s (`NotFoundError`, `InsertedEvent`). A call also takes
`idempotency_key=`, a `confirm` method `passkey=` (else the client's own), and a
view `consistency=` and `min_index=`.

## How the types come out

`u64` and `i64` are decimal strings and `bytes` base64url strings, as on the
wire; `option<T>` is `T | null` (`Optional[T]`) and an optional argument may be
left out. The full table is in [App interface](/core/build/app-abi/#types).

<Aside type="caution">
  ABI version 1 names your own types (a record, a serde struct or enum) without
  their fields, so the client types them `unknown` (`Any`): cast or validate the
  value where you use it.
</Aside>

## Use any OpenAPI tool

`openapi.json` is a standard OpenAPI 3.1 document: each method is
`POST /apps/{app}/methods/{name}`, and its body is `{ args, idempotencyKey? }` for a
call or `{ args, consistency?, minIndex? }` for a view. A running node serves the
same document for an installed app at `GET /apps/{app}/openapi.json`. Generators
and validators read it as they read any other; give the generated code mero-js
or calimero-client-py as its transport, since the node answers only inside the
sealed channel.

## Check a new version before publishing

Compare the new build with the last release:

```bash
mero-app-build abi-diff dist/kv-store-1.0.0.mpk kv-store.wasm
```

```
breaking   method get: result changed: option<string> -> string
compatible method count: added (view)
```

It exits `1` when a change breaks existing callers, so it can gate CI. The rules
are in [App interface](/core/build/app-abi/#check-a-new-version-against-the-last).
Signing runs the same check when you name the last release:

```bash
mero-sign sign manifest.json --key release.key --previous dist/kv-store-1.0.0.mpk
python3 -I scripts/pack-component.py --wasm kv-store.wasm --package com.example.kv-store \
  --app-version 1.1.0 --previous dist/kv-store-1.0.0.mpk --out dist/kv-store-1.1.0.mpk
```

Breaking changes are printed as a warning. A state field removed or changed in
kind while the state version stayed the same is refused: bump
`#[app::state(version = N)]` and migrate the data
([Upgrades & state](/core/build/migrations/)).
